name: In Four
starter: # Assignment: In Four — ask for a name and an age,
# then print what that person's age will be in four years.
# See the instructions on the right, then click Test Code.
instructions: Write a program that asks for a name and an age, then predicts the future:
• Ask for the user's name with input("What is your name?") and store it in a variable.
• Ask for the user's age with input("How old are you?") and store it in a variable.
• Add 4 to the age, then print one line in exactly this shape, using a single print(...) with commas like the Welcome assignment:
(That's what it should print if the user enters Ada and 12 — your program must use whatever name and age are actually typed in.)
A space after the question mark in your prompts — "What is your name? " vs. "What is your name?" — is fine either way; the tester accepts both.

Hitting a TypeError? Good — that's the whole point of this assignment. input() always gives you text (a string), even when the user types digits, and Python refuses to add a number to text. "12" + 4 is an error.

You need to cast (convert) the age from a string to a whole number before you can do math with it. Python's built-in int() function does exactly that — it turns text like "12" into the number 12. Think about where in your program the conversion needs to happen.
The tester runs your program twice with different names and ages, so the math has to really happen — printing a hardcoded answer won't pass.
